declared_purpose: Reduce OpenClaw AI costs through model routing, configurable heartbeats, lean session context, prompt caching and budget controls, with analysis, verification, previews, rollback and estimated savings reports. Backups before modification and preview by default are explicit promises; particular tracking fields, report persistence and memory contents are implementation choices (SKILL.md:26–54,64–86).

data_operations.data_scope: Complete JSON, potentially including credentials if present. Analysis and verification inspect selected optimization settings; optimization preserves other settings through merging.
data_operations.condition: Analysis searches three home-directory paths and two current-directory paths. Optimizer, verifier and health use ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json.

data_operations.source: Workspace files, prompt-file paths and configuration backups
data_operations.data_scope: Existence, filenames and byte sizes. These checks do not read workspace document contents.
data_operations.condition: Analyzer checks seven named files in the current directory and home workspace; verifier checks SOUL.md, USER.md and the optimization prompt; health totals regular workspace files; rollback --list reports backup names and sizes.

data_operations.operation: Infer and report optimization status and savings
data_operations.source: Configuration settings, workspace sizes and fixed cost/traffic assumptions
data_operations.data_scope: Model/provider classification, context-size estimates, budgets, optimization status and projected savings. These are estimates, not measured API usage or billing records.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Diagnostic stdout; analysis results also return to their caller
data_operations.condition: During analyze, verify and health. Analyzer results include a timestamp, configuration path and workspace metadata.

data_operations.data_scope: Timestamp, configuration path, workspace filenames/sizes, model/provider/cache settings, budget amounts, status and inferred savings; not the entire raw configuration.
data_operations.condition: Every successful analyzer main execution, including cli.py analyze; no --apply or output-file option is required. This is outside the documented ~/.openclaw/ write boundary.

data_operations.source: Loaded configuration, generated defaults and requested provider/model/fallback
data_operations.data_scope: Model routing, caching, heartbeat, rate limits and budgets; full mode also writes optimizer identity/version/time and preserves unrelated existing fields.
data_operations.condition: CLI optimize and setup-heartbeat write with --apply; TokenOptimizer defaults to writing when instantiated directly. setup-heartbeat saves after its reachability check without creating a backup, contrary to the general backup promise.

data_operations.data_scope: Entire existing file, including any credentials or unrelated configuration it contains
data_operations.condition: Existing configuration is copied before optimization and restoration when not dry-running. Full mode invokes backup creation twice through optimize_mode. Dry-run still creates the backup directory.

data_operations.operation: Read and restore a selected configuration backup
data_operations.source: A named backup or another supplied existing path
data_operations.data_scope: Entire selected JSON file, first parsed for validity and then copied
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Validation process memory and ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json; current configuration is backed up first
data_operations.condition: rollback --to restores immediately without --apply because its TokenOptimizer instance uses the writing default. --list only enumerates backups.

data_operations.operation: Display configuration values in a diff
data_operations.source: Complete old and proposed configuration dictionaries
data_operations.data_scope: Changed lines and surrounding unchanged context, potentially including sensitive values when they occur in those lines
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Stdout received by the invoking caller or terminal
data_operations.condition: Dry-run save_config serializes both configurations and prints a unified diff without redaction. This is caller-visible output, not an explicit remote transmission.

data_operations.operation: Generate local workspace and prompt files
data_operations.data_scope: Agent rules and placeholders for name, timezone, working hours, mission and metrics; generation does not collect actual profile values. The richer packaged USER.md is a separate manual template.
data_operations.condition: Full optimization writes missing files when applying and skips existing files. Directories are created even in dry-run; printed generated paths reveal the local home path to the caller.

data_operations.source: Provider selection and local executable availability
data_operations.data_scope: GET request and connection metadata; no prompt, configuration body or explicit credential header is added. GROQ_API_KEY is only mentioned in printed setup instructions.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Ollama at http://localhost:11434, LM Studio at http://localhost:1234, or Groq at https://api.groq.com; reachability boolean returns to caller
data_operations.condition: Provider setup, health and callable check helpers can probe even during preview. Ollama requires its executable to be found first. Setup can try a fallback; none skips probing. Full optimization and heartbeat mode explicitly call Ollama setup.

data_operations.source: Configured heartbeat provider and optional heartbeat.endpoint
data_operations.data_scope: Request to the configured URL, including its path/query if present; no explicit configuration payload or credential header is added
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: For lmstudio/groq, the configured endpoint or their default URL; for ollama, fixed localhost:11434. Reachability is reported locally.
data_operations.condition: Verification of a configured heartbeat other than none. Unlike health/setup checks, this verifier honors endpoint overrides for lmstudio/groq.

data_operations.operation: Configure future model, cache and heartbeat processing
data_operations.source: Generated configuration or manually adopted packaged configuration
data_operations.data_scope: Anthropic model identifiers, cache flags and a five-minute TTL; hourly heartbeat prompt, main session and selected provider/endpoint/fallback. Actual session payloads are unspecified.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local OpenClaw configuration; intended downstream processors include configured model services and Ollama, LM Studio or Groq
data_operations.condition: Only if the host later consumes these settings. Full mode deep-merges, so existing heartbeat provider, endpoint or notification target can survive. Selective heartbeat setup replaces the section; provider none removes it. This package does not implement model calls, caching or notifications.

data_operations.operation: Instruct an adopting agent to load context and retrieve memory
data_operations.source: SOUL.md, USER.md, IDENTITY.md, today's notes and relevant historical snippets
data_operations.data_scope: Populated profile/business context and daily notes at session start; relevant memory snippets on demand. The packaged profile can include name, role, schedule, mission, metrics, stack and business constraints.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Adopting host agent's session context; memory-tool results may remain with that caller
data_operations.condition: Only when generated rules are added to an agent prompt or packaged templates are manually adopted and followed. No supplied Python code performs these document-content reads or sends them to a model.

data_operations.operation: Instruct an adopting agent to persist daily memory
data_operations.source: Session work, decisions, generated leads, blockers and next steps
data_operations.data_scope: Daily summaries of those categories; the SOUL template lists work, decisions, blockers and next steps
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md in the host agent's unspecified base directory
data_operations.condition: At session end if the host adopts and follows the rules. This is a persistence instruction, not an implemented write by the optimizer.

data_operations.operation: Persist reporting timestamps and a counter
data_operations.source: Local clock, existing statistics and calculated savings
data_operations.data_scope: installed_at, last_optimized, last_benefit_report and verify_count; activity duration and accumulated savings are inferred. verify_count increments when a report is displayed, not on every verification.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: ~/.openclaw/token-optimizer-stats.json; benefit report and donation URL on stdout
data_operations.condition: Full optimization reads existing stats even in dry-run and writes when applying. Verification writes report time/count without --apply after at least seven active days and seven days since the previous report. Printing the donation URL does not fetch it.

data_operations.operation: Read public package metadata and output preferences
data_operations.source: Packaged version file, README.md, NO_COLOR and stdout terminal status
data_operations.data_scope: Public version/description text and a color-output preference; no API credential environment variable is read here
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local packaging process and color-formatting logic
data_operations.condition: setup.py reads version/README during packaging; colors.py reads NO_COLOR on import and checks terminal status when formatting.

data_operations.operation: Create, inspect, overwrite and delete simulation data
data_operations.source: Synthetic configuration, profile/history text and files under test/mock_environment
data_operations.data_scope: Mock configuration/document contents, file sizes and simulated cost estimates
data_operations.condition: Running simulation_test.py deletes any pre-existing mock_environment tree, creates mocks, overwrites mock config/SOUL/USER, deletes mock MEMORY.md and removes the tree on normal completion. It does not run the production optimizer against the user's home configuration.

potential_excess.data_scope: The complete derived analysis report, including configuration path, workspace metadata, budget amounts and estimated savings
potential_excess.condition: Every analyzer main execution automatically persists the report in the current directory.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Analysis and reporting are declared; automatic persistence is an implementation choice. This is an additional storage action beyond displaying or returning the required diagnostics.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Inspect settings and provide optimization opportunities and estimates to the caller.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Make saving opt-in through an explicit output option; return and display diagnostics by default. Omit the absolute configuration path from exports unless needed.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep requested report export available and retain enough source identification to distinguish configurations.

potential_excess.data_scope: A repeated copy of the entire existing configuration, including any credentials
potential_excess.condition: optimize_mode('full') backs up before calling optimize_full(), which backs up again. Calls within one second can overwrite the same backup filename; otherwise they can create two copies.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: A pre-modification backup is explicitly required. The second backup action is redundant.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Preserve one complete original configuration before the full optimization modifies it.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Dispatch full mode before the outer backup/load, or make exactly one layer responsible for backup creation.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain one successful complete backup before each actual configuration modification and preserve rollback support.

potential_excess.data_scope: Sensitive old/new configuration values and unrelated adjacent values appearing in diff context
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Dry-run stdout delivered to the invoking caller or terminal
potential_excess.condition: Changed sections or surrounding lines contain credentials or other private configuration. Whole model/heartbeat sections can be replaced, and diff generation performs no redaction.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: A meaningful change preview is explicit; printing sensitive values is extra data within that required action.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Show which settings change and their operational effect.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Redact sensitive fields in both configurations before diffing and limit output to relevant changed settings.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Continue showing model/provider choices, cache settings, budgets and other safe values needed to review the change.

potential_excess.data_scope: Task-irrelevant profile/business fields and the complete current daily note
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Adopting host agent's startup context; further model disclosure is unresolved
potential_excess.condition: The startup rule is adopted and populated USER.md or daily notes contain information unrelated to the current task.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Lean session context is explicit. Loading every field in these documents on every session is a template choice.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Supply the preferences and continuity information needed for the current task.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Keep a minimal startup profile and retrieve other profile fields or note snippets when relevant.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Load information needed for the user's task, communication preferences and unresolved work; retain fuller context when explicitly needed.

potential_excess.data_scope: Completed work, decisions, generated leads and other session details beyond future continuity needs
potential_excess.condition: An adopting agent follows the unconditional end-of-session note rule.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Daily notes support reduced context loading; recording every listed category is a template choice rather than an explicit cost-reduction requirement.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Preserve enough state to resume relevant work without loading full history.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Record concise unresolved decisions, blockers and next actions; avoid unnecessary personal/lead identifiers and offer fuller archives only when requested.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep details required to resume unfinished tasks and any records the user explicitly requests.

potential_excess.condition: Full optimization records last_optimized and initializes the counter; due benefit reports increment verify_count.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Savings reports are declared. Supplied reporting logic uses installation/report dates and estimated savings, but does not use these two fields to calculate or schedule reports.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Retain installation time and the last report time for accumulated estimates and weekly cadence.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Stop initializing/updating last_optimized and verify_count unless a user-visible feature requires them.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve installed_at and last_benefit_report so existing report timing and estimates continue working.

potential_excess.data_scope: Ollama executable availability and local service reachability
potential_excess.condition: Heartbeat-only optimization resolves an existing lmstudio/groq provider or disables heartbeat, but then unconditionally calls setup_ollama_heartbeat().
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Provider setup supports heartbeat optimization. Checking an unused local provider is a redundant action for these paths.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Check the provider actually selected, or skip setup when heartbeat is disabled.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Call provider-specific setup for the resolved provider and skip probes for none.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain Ollama checks when Ollama is selected and retain appropriate checks for other selected providers.

unknowns: OpenClaw runtime source is absent. Actual model payloads, main-session heartbeat context, notifications, cache placement/retention and deletion remain unresolved; configuration alone does not establish these operations.
Actual user configuration and document contents are absent. Credential exposure in backups/diffs, task relevance of profile fields and retained heartbeat targets/endpoints are conditional.
memory_search(), memory_get() and host memory-writing implementations are absent. Their backends, recipients, base directory, access controls and retention remain unresolved.
External endpoint logging, retention and further processing are undocumented. The supplied probes establish request targets, not external handling.
Backup/report/statistics retention periods and protective permissions are unspecified. No production cleanup policy is supplied; simulation deletion does not establish deletion of production data.
